`whatsappaudioR` converts compressed mobile voice notes -- the `.opus`/`.ogg`
files produced by WhatsApp and similar VoIP messaging apps -- directly into
tidy data frames ready for analysis. This vignette walks through the core
path: **voice note -> tidy spectrogram -> plot**.

## Reading a voice note

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(whatsappaudioR)

w <- wa_read("voice_note.opus")
w
```

`wa_read()` detects the file extension and, for compressed formats, decodes
via a system `ffmpeg` binary into a `tuneR::Wave` object -- the same
representation you'd get from `tuneR::readWave()` on a plain `.wav` file, so
the rest of the R audio ecosystem (`tuneR`, `seewave`) works on it unchanged.

## Tidy spectrogram

```{r, eval = FALSE}
spec_df <- wa_spectrogram(w, wl = 1024)
head(spec_df)
```

```
#> # A tibble: 6 x 3
#>    time  freq amplitude
#>   <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 0.032 0.000     -38.2
#> 2 0.032 0.016     -41.7
#> ...
```

`freq` is in kHz (matching `seewave`'s convention); `amplitude` is in dB.
Because the result is a long-format tibble, it plots directly with
`ggplot2`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(spec_df, aes(x = time, y = freq, fill = amplitude)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(x = "Time (s)", y = "Frequency (kHz)", fill = "Amplitude (dB)")
```

## Spectral features

```{r, eval = FALSE}
wa_features(w)
```

Returns a one-row tibble of documented spectral features (peak frequency,
spectral centroid, flatness, entropy, rolloff, dominant-frequency stability,
a harmonic-energy heuristic, and 12 MFCCs) -- see `?wa_features` for exact
definitions. Nothing here is a black box: every column is a named,
inspectable, conventional bioacoustic/audio feature.

## Simulating compression

If you have clean, uncompressed audio and want to know how it would sound
(and measure) after passing through a WhatsApp-style pipeline:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
clean <- wa_read("clean_recording.wav")
degraded <- wa_simulate_compression(clean, bitrate = 16000, sr = 16000)
```

This requires a system `ffmpeg` build with `libopus` support.

## Batch processing

```{r, eval = FALSE}
features_df <- wa_batch("voice_notes/", wa_features)
```

Applies any function of a `Wave` object (default `wa_features()`) across
every supported audio file in a directory, returning one row per file with
a `file` column.
